rows.text: Life is mana in this deck. Gwenom's attack trigger turns the top of your library into a hand you pay for in life instead of mana, and she is a lifelinking deathtoucher, so attacking refills the resource she spends. K'rrik does the same thing for every black pip in your costs. Once both are down, your life total is a second mana pool worth twenty or thirty.

rows.name: Gwenom, Remorseless
rows.text: 4/4 deathtouch lifelink, and every attack lets you play off the top of your library, paying LIFE equal to mana value rather than mana. She is Bolas's Citadel that also hits for four and gains it back.

rows.name: Bolas's Citadel
rows.text: the permanent version, and it does not need to attack. Its sacrifice ability is a ten-life drain on each opponent as a finisher.

rows.name: K'rrik, Son of Yawgmoth
rows.text: every {B} in every cost can be paid with two life instead. With him out, Exsanguinate, Gray Merchant and the tutors all cost only their generic portion.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste so Gwenom attacks the turn she lands, and shroud against the removal aimed at her.

rows.name: Swiftfoot Boots
rows.text: hexproof and haste when you need to target her.

rows.name: Lavaspur Boots
rows.text: one mana, haste and ward — the cheapest way to make her connect immediately.

rows.name: Bloodthirsty Conqueror
rows.text: you gain life equal to every point an opponent loses. With a drain spell it is enormous, and it makes the life you spent free.

rows.name: Exquisite Blood
rows.text: the same effect on an enchantment.

rows.name: Sheoldred, the Apocalypse
rows.text: two life per card you draw, two lost per card they draw.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: gains life on every spell, scaling with your storm count, then converts fifty life into fifty damage at any target. In a deck that gains life this fast, that is a real kill.

rows.name: Gray Merchant of Asphodel
rows.text: your devotion to black is high, and the drain is also lifegain.

rows.name: Crypt Ghast
rows.text: doubles every Swamp AND extorts on every spell.

rows.name: Exsanguinate
rows.text: X to each opponent, and you gain all of it back.

rows.name: Dark Ritual
rows.text: three black for one.

rows.name: Cabal Ritual
rows.text: five with threshold on, which this deck reaches quickly.

rows.name: Culling the Weak
rows.text: four black for one mana and a spare body.

rows.name: Rain of Filth
rows.text: turns every land you control into a black mana at once. It is a one-card explosive turn — and lands sacrificed this way are gone, so use it on the turn you win.

rows.name: Blood Pet
rows.text: a body that becomes a ritual.

rows.name: Lotus Petal
rows.text: fixing and acceleration for free.

rows.name: Mox Amber
rows.text: live as soon as Gwenom or K'rrik is out.

rows.name: Mox Opal
rows.text: metalcraft is easy with the Moxen and the Reservoir.

rows.name: Jet Medallion
rows.text: a discount on every card in the deck.

rows.name: Necropotence
rows.text: the best card in the deck. Pay one life per card, as many as you like, with no upper limit — and this deck has three separate ways to gain the life back.

rows.name: Peer into the Abyss
rows.text: half your library into your hand. With K'rrik and rituals down, that is usually the turn you win.

rows.name: Doom Whisperer
rows.text: two life per surveil 2, digging as deep as you need for the missing piece.

rows.name: Night's Whisper
rows.text: two cards for two life.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, all paid in life.

rows.name: Insatiable Avarice
rows.text: a tutor to the top and a three-card draw on the same card.

rows.name: Vampiric Tutor
rows.text: two life for any card in the deck, and Gwenom can cast it off the top the same turn.

rows.name: Grim Tutor
rows.text: straight to hand.

rows.name: Beseech the Mirror
rows.text: bargain it and cast the tutored card free if it costs four or less.

rows.name: Diabolic Intent
rows.text: any card for a spare creature.

rows.name: Razaketh, the Foulblooded
rows.text: a tutor every time you sacrifice a creature, repeatedly, within a single turn.

rows.name: Scheming Symmetry
rows.text: one mana, and you cast yours off the top first while their card sits there.

rows.name: Doomsday
rows.text: five cards, stacked in the exact order you need. It costs half your life, which this deck is uniquely equipped to pay.

rows.name: Scroll Rack
rows.text: swaps a dead hand for the top of your library — and the top of your library is where Gwenom and Bolas's Citadel play from.

rows.name: Sensei's Divining Top
rows.text: sets the top three, so the free casts never whiff.

rows.name: Tendrils of Agony
rows.text: with rituals and free casts, the storm count on a real turn is six or more. That is twelve or more drain and twelve life back.

rows.name: Professor Onyx
rows.text: two drain and two gain on every instant and sorcery you cast OR COPY.

rows.name: Chain of Smog
rows.text: with Professor Onyx on the battlefield, target YOURSELF. Each copy triggers magecraft, and once your hand is empty the discard does nothing — so you copy it as many times as you need and drain the table out. Two cards, and it ends the game on the spot.

rows.name: Aetherflux Reservoir
rows.text: the other kill. Fifty life to the face of whoever is closest to winning.

rows.name: Bolas's Citadel
rows.text: sacrifice ten nonland permanents and every opponent loses ten.

rows.name: Exsanguinate
rows.text: the clean, uninteractive finish when you have the mana.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out.

rows.name: Snuff Out
rows.text: four life instead of four mana, which in this deck is a discount.

rows.name: Infernal Grasp
rows.text: two mana, kills anything.

rows.name: Dismember
rows.text: one mana and four life, or three mana.

rows.name: Feed the Swarm
rows.text: mono-black's only clean enchantment removal.

rows.name: Toxic Deluge
rows.text: a wrath that scales past indestructible, and paying life for it is on-plan.

rows.name: Damnation
rows.text: the unconditional version.

rows.name: Imp's Mischief
rows.text: redirects the removal spell aimed at Gwenom back at something of theirs, or turns their tutor into yours.

rows.name: Defense Grid
rows.text: everything costs three more except on its controller's turn. Your combo turn becomes untouchable.

rows.name: Dauthi Voidwalker
rows.text: unblockable, blanks their graveyards, and steals their best card.

rows.name: Umbral Collar Zealot
rows.text: a free sacrifice outlet that surveils, which sets up both Gwenom and Reanimate.

rows.name: Reanimate
rows.text: one mana for anything in any graveyard.

rows.name: Animate Dead
rows.text: the second copy.

rows.name: The Soul Stone
rows.text: once harnessed, a creature back from the graveyard every upkeep.

rows.name: Boggart Trawler
rows.text: graveyard hate on a body, or a land when you needed the land.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep fast black mana. Dark Ritual, Sol Ring, Lotus Petal and a tutor beats a hand of expensive drain spells — this deck wins by having eight mana on turn four, not by curving out.

Watch your life total as a mana pool, but keep a floor. Between Necropotence, K'rrik, Gwenom and the tutors it is very easy to spend yourself to five with no lifelink attack available. Deploy a lifegain piece before you start burning down.

rows.name: Gwenom, Remorseless
rows.text: attack with her even into a bad board. Deathtouch means blocking is a bad trade for them, lifelink refills you, and the top-of-library access for the turn is worth more than the four damage.

rows.name: Chain of Smog
rows.text: hold it. It is a dead card without Professor Onyx and a game-winner with her, and telegraphing it early just invites the graveyard hate that stops the Reanimate half of the deck too.
